summary: Disclosed remote-agent runner with WebRTC-driven shell execution and bundled reverse-tunnel binaries
details: The package installs a daemon (`factiii-runner start`) that pairs with a vendor account and accepts commands over WebRTC from api.factiii.com to run coding agents (Claude/Codex) in tmux-managed shell sessions on the installer's host, driving arbitrary native builds, simulators and host toolchains. A remote party authenticated to the paired account can therefore execute code on the host. The capability is advertised in README and package.json as the product's core purpose; the daemon starts only on explicit foreground invocation after an interactive browser-pairing step that provisions a JWT, with an optional connection password unlocking the data key at each restart. There is no npm lifecycle hook and no top-level import side effect — install and require do not open the channel. The outbound control plane (api.factiii.com) is the publisher's own documented domain. The tarball also ships four prebuilt `frpc` (Fast Reverse Proxy client) binaries under `vendor/` (linux/darwin × amd64/arm64) wired to a documented `factiii-expose <port> <name>` skill that publishes any local port to the public internet via the vendor's edge as an unauthenticated HTTPS URL; this is invoked only by explicit user/agent command. No reads of `~/.aws`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.npmrc`, browser profiles, wallets, or environment-wide secrets are present, no second undisclosed channel is wired, and the control plane matches the stated publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
